relevance_rationale: The stated reason this case was submitted is HLA-restricted immunotherapy after a second transplant. HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1 and PRAME approaches each name a restricting allele, usually HLA-A*02:01, so the genotype decides whether that entire class of options is open or closed.

profile.json:targetable_features[] HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME)
hardening_gap: High-resolution typing was performed for the 2020 sibling transplant, but no allele-level call sits in the record on hand, so nothing can be acted on. Closing this means retrieving the 4-digit A, B and C type from the transplant and donor-registry file, and repeating typing on a fresh blood draw if the archived report cannot be produced quickly. Type the sibling donor in the same pass, since HA-1/HA-2 eligibility depends on the donor as well as the patient.

therapeutic_implication.approval_status: Product-specific; each names its restricting allele
therapeutic_implication.notes: In AML the relevant programs are HA-1/HA-2-directed TCR-T and PRAME- and WT1-directed approaches. None carries an AML approval.

rationale: Every HLA-restricted option in this case sits behind a genotype that was generated in 2020 but is not in the record on hand. Retrieving or repeating it costs a blood draw and decides whether HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T and PRAME- or WT1-directed approaches are candidates at all, and if A*02:01 is negative, whether A*24:02 opens the alternative WT1 lever. Leave it unresolved and the question this case was submitted to answer cannot be answered, while every HLA-presented antigen below stays unassessable rather than negative.
notes: WT1 and the HA-1/HA-2 minor histocompatibility antigens are named in profile.json:targetable_features[] but appear in neither reference panel, so they carry no survey row. Their measurement status still has to be worked by the target validator directly from the profile, and both sit behind this same genotype. Donor typing is not optional here: HA-1-directed TCR-T requires recipient HA-1(H)-positive with an HA-1-negative donor, and HLA-identical siblings can still differ at that locus.
